correctness.rationale: Orthogonal distinct-prime monomials yield <Ce_m,Ce_n>=(mn)^(−1/2−A−delta)prod_j I0(2a_j sqrt(log m log n)), hence the exact nonnegative double Gram/Schatten-four trace. For delta>0, I0(z)<=e^z and 2sqrt(tu)<=t+u bound by (mn)^(−1−2delta). At delta=0 the weighted-harmonic sum vs logarithmic Lebesgue double integral has a C¹ correction: the measure sum 1/n at log n differs from dt by constant plus exponentially decaying integration-by-parts primitive; derivatives of the Bessel kernel are controlled after boundary terms, so the correction is O(delta). Diagonal change x=(t+u)/2,v=(t−u)/sqrt(x), Jacobian sqrt(x), Bessel I0 asymptotic and Gaussian domination yield Q_d(x)~K_d x^(1/2−d), K_d=(4pi)^(−d)(prod a_j)^(−1)sqrt(2pi/A). Abelian Laplace analysis gives d1 coefficient 1/(4sqrt2 a1^(3/2)) of delta^(−1/2), d2 difference 4sqrt(pi)K2 sqrt(delta), d>=3 derivative 2L_d delta by exact positive series. K2 at a1=a2=1 gives 1/(4pi). Independent scaled-Bessel diagonal profile quadrature at x=1200 gave ratios 1.00013,1.00027,1.00053,1.01489 for four tested amplitude vectors, compatible with non-uniform small-amplitude convergence. Finite profile checks do not replace the integration-by-parts/Abelian proof.
